case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses Bluetooth RF PHY qualification failures caused by transmit output power measurements that only satisfied Class 2 requirements while the target qualification design used a Class 1 Link Layer QDID. The testing team discovered during review that the DUT output power measured approximately 8.6 dBm to 9.2 dBm, which failed the Class 1 minimum threshold. The consultants coordinated with the customer and wireless technology vendor to determine whether firmware transmit power settings could be adjusted to achieve compliant Class 1 output levels. The discussion also clarified which existing RF qualification evidence remained reusable and which tests required retesting.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical discussion focused on the mismatch between the Class 1 Link Layer qualification target and the measured RF PHY transmit power performance. The consultants explained that RF PHY qualification evidence for a Class 1 design requires transmit output power of at least 10 dBm, while the measured DUT only passed Class 2 limits. The thread also examined whether BlueTest3 configuration settings, especially the Int parameter, and firmware transmit power settings affected the measured output power results. Another important point was that RF PHY retesting was mandatory, while previously completed RF testing evidence remained valid because the RF report already satisfied separate Class 1 RF criteria.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's core reasoning was that qualification evidence must match the Bluetooth power class and capabilities of the referenced QDID and Link Layer design. Since the referenced design was a Class 1 implementation, RF PHY output power evidence generated under effective Class 2 conditions could not be used for valid qualification registration. The consultants therefore required firmware changes or updated DUT configurations to raise output power above the Class 1 threshold before RF PHY evidence could be accepted.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the Class 1 and Class 2 distinction is misunderstood, invalid RF PHY evidence may be submitted for qualification, causing qualification rejection, retesting delays, firmware rework, and additional coordination with test labs and module vendors. Failing to verify firmware transmit power settings before testing can also lead to unnecessary repeat testing cycles. Conversely, unnecessarily repeating all RF testing instead of only the affected RF PHY tests can increase schedule impact and testing costs.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: A clear consultant-side mistake occurred when the original RF PHY testing proceeded under a Class 2 test plan or configuration despite the target design requiring Class 1 qualification evidence. The issue was discovered later during report review, and the consultants corrected it by identifying the Class mismatch, requesting firmware output power changes, clarifying that RF PHY retesting was mandatory, and confirming that the existing RF report could still be reused.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always verify that the RF PHY test plan, DUT firmware configuration, Bluetooth power class, and referenced QDID are fully aligned before testing begins. Small mismatches between Class 1 and Class 2 assumptions can invalidate qualification evidence even when measured RF performance appears otherwise acceptable.
